title: Remittances (Private Transfer Receipts, Quarterly)
description: Private (personal) transfer receipts in India's balance of payments, mainly remittances by Indians working overseas, in US$ billion per quarter. QUARTERLY data from the RBI's balance of payments press release. Remittances finance a large part of the goods trade deficit and support household consumption, especially in Kerala, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh; they respond to Gulf and US labour markets and the rupee.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Developments in India's Balance of Payments, quarterly press release)

qna.question: What does this measure?
qna.answer: Private transfer receipts (called personal transfer receipts since the BPM6 re-labelling), the largest part of secondary income in the current account, mainly money sent home by Indians employed abroad.^This is quarterly data, in US$ billion, for the quarter ending on the date shown.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Use the year-on-year view: remittances grow with the number of overseas workers, wages abroad and the rupee, and fell in 2020 during the pandemic.^Because they are about 3 per cent of GDP they matter for the current account balance: a rise in remittances narrows the current account deficit.

qna.question: Caveats
qna.answer: Figures come from the narrative of RBI's press release (US$ billion, one decimal) rather than the detailed BoP tables, which are published as files on a host that blocks automated downloads. Each quarter's first release is preliminary and is revised later.^Remittances are net of nothing: they are gross receipts, while outward remittances are a separate (smaller) payments item.

note: Quarterly only. Each quarter is taken from the RBI press release for that quarter (preliminary); where a later release states a revised figure for the year-earlier quarter, that revision replaces it. Other quarters keep their first-published values, so older quarters can differ from the RBI's latest BoP tables.
